name: Bulent Eczacibasi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Bulent Eczacibasi and brother Faruk are partners in a conglomerate that has 25 production facilities in Turkey and 16 abroad.
It is a global exporter of ceramic and wall tiles, plus bathroom fixtures and accessories (brands include VitrA, Villeroy & Boch and Engers Keramik).
Bulent and Faruk's father, Dr. Nejat F. Eczacibasi, focused on pharmaceuticals before expanding into personal health care and other businesses.
Eczacibasi Holding also operates in healthcare services and the production and distribution of medical products to hospitals.
Other key sectors are consumer products, finance, IT, mining and real estate development. Eczacibasi is Turkey's leading producer of toilet paper.
forbes_facts: An avid collector, Bulent heads the Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts and the Istanbul Modern Art Foundation, which includes the Istanbul Modern Art Museum.
In Turkish, Eczacibasi means "chief pharmacist," an honorary title and surname given to Bulent's grandfather, Suleyman Ferit Eczacibasi.

name: Rit Thirakomen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2017-2021); Hurun Global (2015-2024)
forbes_bio: Electrical engineer Rit Thirakomen chairs Bangkok-listed MK Restaurant Group known for its value-for-money 'sukiyaki' restaurants.
The restaurant chain was founded by his late mother-in-law as a small Thai eatery in 1962.
After co-founding a book publishing business in 1974, he took to the restaurant trade in 1987, expanding into sukiyaki with wife Yupin.
Today, MK has more than 700 restaurants, including Japanese food chain Yayoi.
forbes_facts: At MK Suki Restaurants customers cook their own food in a hotpot at their table.

name: Lu Bin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2014-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Lu Bin is a director of Neway Valve (Suzhou).
Lu co-founded the company in 1997 with Wang Baoqing, Cheng Zhangwen and Xi Chao.
The company went public in 2014.

name: Pedro Voigt Trejes
forbes_bio: Pedro Voigt Trejes is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
The company was cofounded by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with late billionaires Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus.
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG has annual revenue of approximately $7 billion.
Voigt Trejes does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; his brother and younger sister are also major shareholders.

name: Waldemar Munich
forbes_bio: Waldemar Munich is the CEO of Spitzke, a German railway construction business.
Spitzke was founded in 1936 by Alfred Spitzke, three years before the start of WWII.
The company started in Breslau, Germany as a railway track layer and moved to Berlin in 1946.
Spitzke expaned into other European countries in the 1990s, shortly after Munich joined the management team in 1991.

name: Johannes Kaercher
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2016-2019); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Johannes Kaercher owns 50% of the world's largest privately held cleaning equipment company, Alfred Kaercher GmbH & Co. KG.
Ownership transferred to him and his sister Susanne Zimmerman von Siefart years after the death of their father Alfred, who founded Kaercher in 1935.
Although not involved in the active management of the company, Kaercher chairs its supervisory board.
The company employs over 12,300 people and generates more than $2.8 billion in annual revenue.
forbes_facts: In 1950, the company created the first European hot-water pressure washer.
Kaercher is Protestant, and he gave the Reformation Day sermon at Berlin's St. Matthew's Church (Matthaeuskirche) in 2016.

name: Ritesh Arora
appears_on: Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2022-2023); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)

name: Zhang Yubai
forbes_bio: Zhang Yubai chairs rice wine supplier Yanghe Group.
He was formally general manager and vice chairman of A-share listed Jiangsu Yanghe Brewery Joint-stock.
Yanghe employs nearly 30,000 people, according to the company's website.

name: M.P. Ramachandran
forbes_bio: M.P. Ramachandran founded consumer goods outfit Jyothy Labs in 1983.
He is now chairman emeritus of the Mumbai company which makes detergents, dishwashing soaps, fabric whiteners and mosquito repellents.
Its flagship brand, Ujala, is a market leader in the fabric whitener segment.
M.R. Jyothy,  the older of his two daughters after whom the company has been named, has been managing director since April 2020.
Ramachandran started his career as an accountant in the early 1970s.
